sentences.zh: 遠跡由斯舉，永世無風塵。

translations.literal: Far footprints rise from this—eternal age without dust of strife.
translations.idiomatic: Distant tracks begin here—endless reign without battle haze.

translations.literal: Song for Troops Returning from Labor Campaign—by Zhang Hua
translations.idiomatic: Homecoming Host after Punitive March—Zhang Hua

sentences.zh: 玁犬允背天德，構亂擾邦畿。

translations.literal: The Xianyun truly betrayed Heaven’s virtue—raising turmoil, harassing royal domain.
translations.idiomatic: Border wolves renounced celestial duty—stirred chaos round the capital belt.

sentences.zh: 戎車震朔野，群帥贊皇威。

translations.literal: War chariots thunder northern wastes—hosts of captains aid imperial awe.
translations.idiomatic: Battle cars shake frontier north—legions of generals magnify royal terror.

sentences.zh: 將士齊心旅，感義忘其私。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers one-hearted on march—moved by duty they forget private gain.
translations.idiomatic: Troops march single-minded—righteousness makes selfish thought dissolve.

sentences.zh: 積勢如郭弩，赴節如發機。

translations.literal: Massed momentum like crossbows drawn full—answering beat like triggers sprung.
translations.idiomatic: Stored force strains like cocked bolt—timing bursts like released latch.

sentences.zh: 囂聲動山谷，金光曜素暉。

translations.literal: Roar shakes mountain valleys—golden gleam flashes pale radiance.
translations.idiomatic: Howl shatters ravines—bronze glare whites dim daylight.

sentences.zh: 揮戈陵勁敵，武步蹈橫屍。

translations.literal: They whirl spears over stubborn foes—martial steps tread sprawled corpses.
translations.idiomatic: Halberds wheel above tough enemies—war strides crush fallen lines.

sentences.zh: 鯨鯢皆授首，北土永清夷。

translations.literal: Leviathans all lose heads—northern soil forever cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Monsters all yield skulls—northern earth stays swept clean.

sentences.zh: 昔往冒隆暑，今來白雪霏。

translations.literal: Once we marched through sweltering heat—now we return through flying snow.
translations.idiomatic: We left in blistering summer—we enter under drifting snow.

sentences.zh: 征夫信勤瘁，自古詠《采薇》。

translations.literal: Campaign men truly toil and waste—since antiquity singers chant “Picking Fern-heads.”
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers know ache and exhaustion—ages hence poets sing “Gathering Ferns.”

sentences.zh: 收榮于舍爵，燕喜在凱歸。

translations.literal: Harvested glory rests in setting cups—feast joy waits in triumph home.
translations.idiomatic: Glory gathered when goblets lower—banquet gladness crowns victorious return.

translations.literal: Song for the Inner Palace—by Zhang Hua
translations.idiomatic: Empress Quarter Hymn—Zhang Hua

sentences.zh: 先王統大業，玄化漸八維。

translations.literal: Former kings threaded great enterprise—dark transformation seeped eight dimensions.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient sovereigns bound mega-work—subtle reform soaked eight poles.

sentences.zh: 儀刑孚萬邦，內訓隆壼闈。

translations.literal: Model and law won myriad states—inner instruction exalted inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Pattern and statute swayed all realms—domestic teaching honored queen’s chambers.

sentences.zh: 皇英垂帝典，《大雅》詠三妃。

translations.literal: Huang and Ying hung imperial canon—“Greater Elegantiae” sings three consorts.
translations.idiomatic: Royal heroines draped dynastic standard—“Greater Ya” hymns three brides.

sentences.zh: 執德宣隆教，正位理厥機。

translations.literal: Grasping virtue they broadcast lofty teaching—correct station ordered its pivots.
translations.idiomatic: Clutching merit they spread high doctrine—rightful seat tuned its gears.

sentences.zh: 含章體柔順，帥禮蹈謙祗。

translations.literal: Holding culture they embodied supple obedience—leading ritual they trod humble awe.
translations.idiomatic: With inward pattern they wore yielding grace—guiding ceremony they walked shy reverence.

translations.literal: “Locusts” magnifies kindness and grace—“Stooping Bough” reaches hidden subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: “Locusts” amplifies mercy—“Tumbling Branch” touches quiet depths.

sentences.zh: 徽音穆清風，高義邈不追。

translations.literal: Fine voices breeze clear wind—high righteousness far beyond pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Bright echoes ride fresh gale—lofty duty beyond chasing.

sentences.zh: 遺榮參日月，百世仰餘暉。

translations.literal: Renouncing glory they rival sun and moon—hundred ages gaze up at afterglow.
translations.idiomatic: Yielding fame they match luminaries—centuries lift eyes to lingering glow.

translations.literal: Song for Clan Kinsmen Assembly—by Zhang Hua
translations.idiomatic: Lineage Gathering Hymn—Zhang Hua

sentences.zh: 族燕明禮順，啜食序親親。

translations.literal: Clan feast clarifies ritual compliance—sipping food orders kin with kin.
translations.idiomatic: Family banquet demonstrates courteous order—shared bowls rank blood with blood.

sentences.zh: 骨肉散不殊，昆弟豈他人。

translations.literal: Flesh and bone scattered yet not alien—brothers how could they be other men?
translations.idiomatic: Joint and marrow parted yet kin—how could cousins count as strangers?

sentences.zh: 本枝篤同慶，《棠棣》著先民。

translations.literal: Root and branches share deep gladness—“Pear Tree” hymn marks ancient folk.
translations.idiomatic: Trunk and twigs taste joint joy—“Pear Blossom” ode recalls ancestors.

sentences.zh: 于皇聖明後，天覆弘且仁。

translations.literal: Oh bright sage succeeding throne—Heaven’s mantle vast and humane.
translations.idiomatic: O luminous heir who took mandate—sky canopy wide and kind.

sentences.zh: 降禮崇親戚，旁施協族姻。

translations.literal: Lowering ritual they honor kin—spreading kindness harmonizes clan marriages.
translations.idiomatic: They humble ceremony for relatives—extend grace to in-law ties.

sentences.zh: 式宴盡酣娛，飲禦備羞珍。

translations.literal: Thus feast exhausts merry ease—drinking and shield rites prepare rare delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: Banquet drains joyful leisure—cup and escort rites heap savories.

sentences.zh: 和樂既宣洽，上下同歡欣。

translations.literal: Harmonious music already proclaimed concord—high and low share gladness.
translations.idiomatic: Concordant sound already sealed unity—above and below rejoice together.

sentences.zh: 德教加四海，敦睦被無垠。

translations.literal: Virtuous teaching reaches four seas—cordial friendship mantles without bound.
translations.idiomatic: Moral instruction crosses four oceans—warm peace drapes past horizon.

sentences.zh: 泰始九年，光祿大夫荀勖以杜夔所制律呂，校太樂、總章、鼓吹八音，與律呂乖錯，乃制古尺，作新律呂，以調聲韻。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taishi, Minister Guanglu Xun Xu, because the pitch pipes Du Kui had devised—when checked against Grand Music, General Regulation, and Drum-and-Bugle eight timbres—clashed with standard lu, then fashioned ancient foot-rules and cast new pitch tubes to tune modes and intervals.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi 9 saw Xun Xu compare Du Kui’s pitch system with palace ensembles and martial bands; finding mismatch, he cast archaic rods and new tubes to true the scale.

translations.literal: The matter is fully recorded in the “Treatise on Pitch Pipes and the Calendar.”
translations.idiomatic: Full detail appears in the treatise on harmonics and calendrics.

sentences.zh: 律成，遂班下太常，使太樂、總章、鼓吹、清商施用。

translations.literal: Once the pipes were complete, orders went down to the Chamberlain of Ceremonial for Grand Music, General Regulation, Drum-and-Bugle, and Pure Shop to adopt them.
translations.idiomatic: Finished scales were promulgated to the Ministry of Rites for adoption by court music bureaus.

sentences.zh: 勖遂典知樂事，啟朝士解音律者共掌之。

translations.literal: Xun Xu then supervised musical affairs and memorialized that court gentlemen who grasped pitch theory should jointly administer them.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu took charge of performance and asked literati who understood temperament to co-manage it.

sentences.zh: 使郭夏、宋識等造《正德》、《大豫》二舞，其樂章亦張華之所作雲。

translations.literal: He assigned Guo Xia, Song Shi, and others to create the two dances “Correct Virtue” and “Grand Ease”—their lyrics likewise composed by Zhang Hua.
translations.idiomatic: He tasked Guo Xia and Song Shi with choreography for “Zhengde” and “Dayu”—lyrics again from Zhang Hua.

translations.literal: Correct Virtue Dance Song—by Zhang Hua
translations.idiomatic: “Zhengde” Dance Hymn—Zhang Hua

translations.literal: Sun august, Heaven high—dark mirror alone sheds light.
translations.idiomatic: Solar lord aloft—shadowy scrutiny alone shines.

translations.literal: Sacred regalia cycles round—five powers replace in splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Divine tokens wheel—five virtues take rotating glory.

translations.literal: Fortune’s mandate rests with Jin—ages hold wise kings.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven’s lot settles on Jin—successions seat sagely rulers.

translations.literal: They broadly succor inner summer—they mold and fire myriad directions.
translations.idiomatic: They rescue central plain—they kiln-fire every quarter.

translations.literal: Great brilliance hangs its glow—side lamps illumine without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Grand splendor lowers gleam—peripheral torches know no bound.

translations.literal: Busy busy common kinds—wind virtue forever strong.
translations.idiomatic: Teeming common folk—custom’s power ever robust.

translations.literal: Imperial path alone is pure—ritual and music are its warp.
translations.idiomatic: The royal way stays lucid—rites and song form its fixed threads.

translations.literal: Metal and stone hang suspended—myriad dancers fill courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Bronze and jade hang ranked—countless dancers pack the yard.

translations.literal: Gestures image blessing—they harmonize pitch and cloak sound.
translations.idiomatic: Figures display fortune—they wed mode and mantle tone.

translations.literal: Surpassing “Wu,” transcending “Hu”—they borrow beat from “Six Ying.”
translations.idiomatic: Leaping past “Grand Wu,” vaulting “Grand Hu”—they steal rhythm from “Six Ying.”

translations.literal: Together advancing, together yielding—transformation seeps beyond shape.
translations.idiomatic: Joint charge, joint retreat—reform trickles past visible form.

translations.literal: Grand harmony proclaimed concord—it penetrates dim netherworld.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme concord spreads—it threads silent shades.

translations.literal: Grand Ease Dance Song—by Zhang Hua
translations.idiomatic: “Dayu” Dance Hymn—Zhang Hua

translations.literal: Such is Heaven’s command—tally and fortune know their return.
translations.idiomatic: Thus runs celestial writ—omens and luck own their course.

translations.literal: Blazing Great Jin—three later lords doubled splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Resplendent mighty Jin—three successors stacked glory.

translations.literal: Continuing brilliance, renewing ages—radiance soothes nine spheres.
translations.idiomatic: Carrying flame, handing eras—gleam nurses nine peripheries.

translations.literal: Our emperor inherits destined season—thus rests upon celestial pivot.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign takes timed mandate—therefore sits on polar hinge.

translations.literal: Myriad lives attach their fate—suddenly possessing hundred domains.
translations.idiomatic: Creatures hang fortunes—swiftly holding myriad states.

translations.literal: Carefully tracing five canons—dark teaching reaches far.
translations.idiomatic: Guardedly honoring five statutes—arcane doctrine bridges distance.

translations.literal: Myriad quarters share one track—all soils join harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand regions ride shared gauge—every soil merges ease.

translations.literal: Thus they fashioned “Grand Ease”—broadcasting virtue through dance merit.
translations.idiomatic: Hence choreographed “Grand Ease”—spreading merit through swaying ode.

translations.literal: Pure transformation already solemn—kingly Way coordinated lofty.
translations.idiomatic: Distilled reform stands grave—royal course aligns with height.

translations.literal: Kindness reaches grass and trees—grace adds even to crawling things.
translations.idiomatic: Mercy touches herb and timber—bounty sinks to creeping kin.

translations.literal: Hundred millions of barbarian folk—joyfully lift eyes to royal breeze.
translations.idiomatic: Countless tribes beyond heartland—gladly crane toward sovereign wind.

translations.literal: Brilliantly manifest great enterprise—forever ages it mounts revered.
translations.idiomatic: Brightly shown mega-work—endless reigns heap reverence.

sentences.zh: 荀勖又作新律笛十二枚，以調律呂，正雅樂，正會殿庭作之，自謂宮商克諧，然論者猶謂勖暗解。

translations.literal: Xun Xu further fashioned twelve new-flute pipes to regulate lu tubes and rectify ritual music; court assemblies in the main hall used them—he claimed gong and shang matched perfectly, yet critics still called Xu’s grasp dim.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu cut twelve fresh panpipes to tune classical pitch for state halls; he insisted modes aligned, though critics sneered his ear was blunt.

sentences.zh: 時阮咸妙達八音，論者謂之神解。

translations.literal: At that time Ruan Xian mastered eight timbres—critics deemed his understanding divine.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Xian meanwhile commanded eight instrumental families—onlookers called his ear heaven-sent.

sentences.zh: 咸常心譏勖新律聲高，以為高近哀思，不合中和。

translations.literal: Xian secretly mocked Xu’s new scales as sharp-high—thinking heights neared mournful thought and broke centered harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan quietly mocked Xu’s sharp tuning—too bright, too close to grief, betraying equipoise.

sentences.zh: 每公會樂作，勖意咸謂之不調，以為異己，乃出咸為始平相。

translations.literal: Whenever public banquets struck up music, Xu suspected Xian meant disharmony—seeing him as rival—and therefore posted Xian out as prefect of Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: Each court feast, Xun heard sabotage in Ruan’s silence—read it mutiny—and banished him as Shiping prefect.

sentences.zh: 後有田父耕于野，得周時玉尺，勖以校己所治鐘鼓金石絲竹，皆短校一米，於此伏咸之妙，復徵咸歸。

translations.literal: Later a farmer tilling wild fields unearthed a Zhou-period jade foot-rule; Xu compared it to bells, drums, metal, stone, silk, and bamboo he had tuned—all proved one chi shorter than his calibration—thus he conceded Xian’s subtlety and recalled him.
translations.idiomatic: Later peasants dug up a Zhou jade yardstick; against it Xu’s orchestra proved uniformly short one chi—then he bowed to Ruan’s finesse and summoned him home.

sentences.zh: 勖既以新律造二舞，次更修正鐘聲。

translations.literal: Xun Xu already used new pipes to fashion the two dances—next he corrected bell pitches.
translations.idiomatic: Having staged both dances on new temperament, Xu moved on to true bell tones.

translations.literal: Just then Xun Xu died—the task stayed unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: He died before finishing the overhaul.

sentences.zh: 元康三年，詔其子籓修定金石，以施郊廟。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuankang an edict ordered his son Fan to finish correcting metal and stone instruments for suburban and temple use.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang 3 commanded his son Fan to complete bronze and lithophone adjustment for suburban shrines.

translations.literal: Soon afterward turmoil struck—none recorded the outcome.
translations.idiomatic: Before long catastrophe swept in—and nobody preserved what followed.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖自蜀漢將定三秦，閬中範因率賨人以從帝，為前鋒。

translations.literal: Han Gaozu, marching from Shu-Han intent on settling Three Qins, was joined by Fan Yin of Langzhong leading Cong tribesmen as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bang pressed east from Ba-Shu to conquer the Three Qin, Fan Yin of Langzhong marched Cong clansmen ahead as his spear-tip.

sentences.zh: 及定秦中，封因為閬中侯，復賨人七姓。

translations.literal: Once Qin heartland was pacified, he ennobled Yin as marquis of Langzhong and restored seven Cong surnames.
translations.idiomatic: After the central plain submitted, Fan Yin became marquis of Langzhong and seven Cong lineages regained noble standing.

sentences.zh: 其俗喜舞，高祖樂其猛銳，數觀其舞，後使樂人習之。

translations.literal: Their custom delighted in dance; Gaozu enjoyed their fierce edge, often watched their performance, later ordered musicians to drill it.
translations.idiomatic: Those folk loved war dance; the founding emperor savored its savage edge, watched often, then told court artists to master it.

sentences.zh: 閬中有渝水，因其所居，故名曰《巴渝舞》。

translations.literal: Langzhong holds the Yu River; because they dwelt there, it was titled “Bayu Dance.”
translations.idiomatic: The Yu River runs through Langzhong; settlers lent their name to what courtiers called the Bayu drill.

sentences.zh: 舞曲有《矛渝本歌曲》、《安弩渝本歌曲》、《安臺本歌曲》、《行辭本歌曲》，總四篇。

translations.literal: The dance suite comprised “Spear-Yu Root Song,” “Rest-Crossbow Yu Root Song,” “Peace-Platform Root Song,” and “March-Lyric Root Song”—four pieces altogether.
translations.idiomatic: The cycle listed four root lyrics—Spear Yu, Rest-the-Crossbow Yu, Quiet Terrace, and Marching Verses—four movements total.

sentences.zh: 其辭既古，莫能曉其句度。

translations.literal: The wording was already archaic—none could grasp its line breaks.
translations.idiomatic: Language hoary as relic—no living reader could parse its caesuras.

sentences.zh: 魏初，乃使軍謀祭酒王粲改創其詞。

translations.literal: Early Wei therefore ordered Army Counsel Superintendent Wang Can to rewrite the lyrics.
translations.idiomatic: Early Wei charged Libationer Wang Can with drafting fresh words.

sentences.zh: 粲問巴渝帥李管、種玉歌曲意，試使歌，聽之，以考校歌曲，而為之改為《矛渝新福歌曲》、《弩渝新福歌曲》、《安台新福歌曲》、《行辭新福歌曲》，《行辭》以述魏德。

translations.literal: Can questioned Bayu instructors Li Guan and Zhong Yu on each tune’s intent, had trial performances listened to, compared scores, then refashioned them as “Spear-Yu New Blessing Song,” “Crossbow-Yu New Blessing Song,” “Terrace New Blessing Song,” and “March-Lyric New Blessing Song”—the march lyric praising Wei virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Can queried drill masters Li Guan and Zhong Yu, auditioned choruses, collated melody, and issued New Blessing versions—March Lyrics hymning Wei power.

sentences.zh: 黃初三年，又改《巴渝舞》曰《昭武舞》。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangchu they again renamed “Bayu Dance” “Manifest Martial Dance.”
translations.idiomatic: Huangchu 3 rechristened Bayu as the Display Martial suite.

sentences.zh: 至景初元年，尚書奏，考覽三代禮樂遺曲，據功象德，奏作《武始》、《咸熙》、《章斌》三舞，皆執羽龠。

translations.literal: By the first year of Jingchu the Secretariat memorialized, reviewing remnant tunes of three dynasties’ ritual music; judging merit and imaging virtue, they submitted choreographing three dances—“Martial Inception,” “Universal Radiance,” and “Patterned Excellence”—all bearing feather-plumes and yue-flutes.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchu 1 brought a memorial comparing Shang-Zhou-Han survivals; weighing deeds against virtue, ministers debuted Martial Inception, All-pervading Dawn, and Pattern Splendor—each dancer clutching plumes and pitch-pipes.

sentences.zh: 及晉又改《昭武舞》曰《宣武舞》，《羽龠舞》曰《宣文舞》。

translations.literal: When Jin succeeded, they renamed “Manifest Martial Dance” “Proclaimed Martial Dance,” and “Plume-Yue Dance” “Proclaimed Civil Dance.”
translations.idiomatic: Jin swapped Display Martial for Proclaimed Martial and rechristened Plume-Yue as Proclaimed Civil choreography.

sentences.zh: 咸甯元年，詔定祖宗之號，而廟樂乃停《宣武》、《宣文》二舞，而同用荀勖所使郭夏、宋識等所造《正德》、《大豫》二舞雲。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianning an edict fixed ancestral temple titles; temple music therefore retired Proclaimed Martial and Proclaimed Civil, universally adopting instead the two dances Guo Xia and Song Shi had fashioned for Xun Xu—“Correct Virtue” and “Grand Ease.”
translations.idiomatic: Xianning 1 sealed shrine honorifics; court orchestras shelved both martial-civil Jin suites and standardized on Xun Xu’s Zhengde and Dayu pieces by Guo Xia and Song Shi.
